classification_note: Exploratory single-reviewer exercise on five constructed cases. It illustrates which artifacts one reviewer inspected; it is not a controlled study, not a reproducible benchmark, and not evidence that defect-detection rates improve in general.
question: Does the Phase 2 review guidance change what a reviewer inspects and reports?

design.environment: isolated git sandbox at /tmp/sem-eval/app (disposable, never committed; the branches no longer exist in this repository)
design.pass_a: diff-focused review under the pre-change templates (git HEAD)
design.pass_b: repository-context review under the Phase 2 templates
design.scoring: seeded defects matched against reported findings; behavioral coverage counts requirements with a behavioral mapping
design.reviewer: single agent, both passes, ground truth known to the experiment author
design.missing_evidence_note: No prompt, transcript, reviewer output, or seed repository was preserved. Only the aggregate counts below survive, so the exercise cannot be rerun or audited case by case.

effort_proxy.note: word count only; no timing, token, or reviewer-hour measurement

baseline_pass_a.precision_note: not computed: per-finding true/false classification was never recorded

effort_proxy.note: word count only; no timing, token, or reviewer-hour measurement

improved_pass_b.precision_note: not computed: per-finding true/false classification was never recorded

limitations: n=5 constructed cases with known ground truth; recall is not an estimate over real changes
single reviewer executed both passes, so order and familiarity can inflate the improvement
pass A is modelled as diff-focused, which understates a careful reviewer using the old template's 'relevant surrounding code' line
no independent second reviewer, no inter-rater reliability, no measure of defect escapes over time
the experiment measures inspection scope and reporting, not semantic correctness of the findings
no per-finding true/false table was kept, so precision cannot be derived from the recorded data
the sandbox and reviewer transcripts were not preserved, so the exercise is not reproducible
interpretation: The guidance changed which artifacts were inspected (callers, tests, specs) and therefore which defects were reported in this exercise. This is an illustration of the guidance's effect on one reviewer, not evidence that defect-detection rates improved in general.
